navy-950.note: The darkest step and the site's primary drench: hero, footer, dark sub-heroes, control sections, lightbox backdrop.

navy-900.note: The brand's primary colour. Primary CTA gradient, interactive elements, resting state of body links.

navy-800.note: Top stop of the primary-button gradient and of ambient section glows.

navy-700.note: Interactive hover/focus on light surfaces: card borders, link underlines, glow washes.

navy-300.note: Secondary text and map labels on dark surfaces; the cold tone of the spark-gap divider.

navy-100.note: Light alternating section background, resting card borders, and body text on navy drenches.

green-500.note: ACCENT ONLY. The logo's leaf. Service-card icons, eyebrow dashes, step numbers, bullets, text selection. Never a background, never a large fill (the Leaf Rarity Rule). The dark steps of this ramp are reference tone only — they were deleted from the palette in DESIGN.md section 0.1 and must not be used as surfaces.

green-400.note: ACCENT ONLY. The 24/7 heartbeat: live dots, telemetry pulse, checkmarks, the coverage-map pin and radius rings. Never a fill larger than a marker.

signal-400.note: The technical signal accent: eyebrow labels and dashes, focus-visible outlines, the spark-gap arc, hover glow on dark CTAs, the coverage-map wash.

tier-basic.note: RCS tier marker, from the company presentation. Top rule and heading of the Basic tier card only.

tier-advance.note: RCS tier marker. Top rule and heading of the Advance tier card only.

tier-pro.note: RCS tier marker. Top rule and heading of the Pro tier card only.

paper.note: Base page background on light sections; text colour on navy drenches.

ink.note: Body text on paper. Muted variants are opacity steps of ink, never a separate gray.

hero.purpose: The homepage H1 only. Archivo with the width axis at 112% and weight 760.

display.purpose: H1 on inner pages. Archivo width axis opened to 125%.

headline.purpose: H2 section titles, Archivo at 125% width, text-wrap: balance.

control.purpose: H2s in the Control Room / RCS narrative. Since section 0.2 it is Archivo at normal width (100%, weight 620) against the Expanded 125% of the field displays — that width contrast, not a colour and no longer a serif, is what marks the control voice. Source Serif 4 has been removed from the project.

body.purpose: Running copy, Inter. Capped at 68ch (.measure) or 54ch (.measure-tight).

button.purpose: Every CTA. A hair under body so a pill reads as a control, not a sentence.

label.purpose: The eyebrow line opening most sections, preceded by a 32x2px dash.

pill-label.purpose: Tags and spec chips inside telemetry panels.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Primary CTAs, light glass panels, the coverage-map card.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Hover-lifted cards and buttons. Always paired with a -2px to -4px translateY.

shadows.name: shadow-glass
shadows.purpose: Dark glass only. The inset top highlight is the specular edge; without it glass reads as flat translucency.

shadows.name: glow-signal
shadows.purpose: Hover glow on dark CTAs and the telemetry monitor. Never at rest.

shadows.name: glow-green
shadows.purpose: Live-state glow on telemetry accents. Marker scale only, per the Leaf Rarity Rule.

motion.name: ease-signature
motion.purpose: The default: an out-quint. All state transitions, reveals, and hover lifts.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The live-dot ping and other one-shot pulses that must decay fast.

motion.name: live-ping
motion.purpose: The 24/7 heartbeat ring expanding out of .ds-live-dot.

motion.name: scan
motion.purpose: The scanline sweeping the RCS monitor screenshot. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
The standard is still the one the client's own 2024 brochure earned — the site should read like the print collateral of a serious electrical-engineering contractor: deep navy, generous white space, confident large-scale type, one signature graphic, not a SaaS product landing page. What changed in 2026-07 is the material, not the posture: surfaces are frosted glass over navy with soft layered depth, rendered with the precision of instrument housing rather than the softness of a consumer app. Restraint is still the default, and it is now enforced by where effects are allowed rather than by banning them outright — blur only where something genuinely floats (the Earned Blur Rule), shadows only in the navy's own shade (the Navy Shadow Rule), green only at the scale of a marker (the Leaf Rarity Rule).

Since 2026-07 the site also has a single surface colour. The green drench that used to mark the control sections (Control Room, RCS, CCI) read as a second brand rather than a second voice, so navy now carries every surface and the dark green steps were deleted from the palette outright. The control world still exists, but it is spoken rather than coloured: a Source Serif 4 authority face, a live 24/7 dot, telemetry panels, a scanline.

Density is generous but purposeful: sections carry one idea each, separated by real vertical space. The one permitted piece of ornament is the spark gap — a Jacob's ladder arc struck between two electrodes, closing every hero. Everything else earns its place through structure rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy + paper-white base, with leaf-green and signal-blue reserved for small, deliberate accents only
Large, confident, geometric-expanded display type paired with a neutral, highly readable body face
Depth from frosted glass and soft layered shadows, tuned to feel engineered rather than decorative
One recurring signature element (the spark gap), not a library of decorative motifs
Mobile-first, touch-parity by construction: nothing shown only on hover

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: Navy is the only surface colour of the site, control sections included. The dark green steps were deleted from the palette so a green section cannot come back by accident. Continuity over contrast.

rules.name: The Leaf Rarity Rule
rules.body: green-500 and green-400 never fill a background, a button, or a section. They appear only as small marks — a live dot, an eyebrow dash, a step number, an icon, a bullet, a map pin — and their rarity is what keeps green feeling like the logo's signature colour rather than a UI colour.

rules.name: The Navy Ramp Rule
rules.body: navy-950 through navy-100 is a single continuous tonal ramp, not six unrelated colours. Any new navy-family need should sit somewhere on this same ramp rather than introducing an unrelated blue.

rules.name: The Navy Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is mixed from rgba(10, 42, 68, ...). A neutral or black shadow anywhere in the system is a bug — on the paper background it reads as smudge rather than depth.

rules.name: The Earned Blur Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter is for elements that genuinely float over something: the navbar island over the hero, captions over photography, the lightbox, telemetry panels over a drench. Glass on a static section against a flat background is decoration, and PRODUCT.md rules out decorative glassmorphism by name.

rules.name: The No-Fluff Rule
rules.body: Copy is short, factual, and technically specific (norms, equipment, kV ratings) rather than motivational. If a sentence could appear on any B2B site regardless of industry, cut it.

rules.name: The Deliberate Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The eyebrow-dash-title pattern is inherited directly from the client's print brochure — it is brand continuity, not a default scaffold. Because a tracked-uppercase kicker above every section is also the most common AI-generated-site tell, treat it as a single system applied consistently rather than as filler reached for per-section; vary section rhythm through spacing, StatBar, marquee, and full-bleed gallery breaks.

dos: Do keep green-500 / green-400 to micro-accents only — a live dot, an eyebrow dash, a step number, an icon, a bullet (the Leaf Rarity Rule).
Do drench every surface in navy, control sections included (the One Surface Rule).
Do mix every shadow from rgba(10, 42, 68, ...) so depth reads as the navy's own shade (the Navy Shadow Rule).
Do write explicit, task-specific button labels ("Chiamaci ora", "Scrivici via email"), never "Invia" / "Submit".
Do cap body copy at 65-68ch measure at every breakpoint.
Do give every CTA the same metrics — 999px pill, 48px min-height, 13px 26px — and change only the material.
Do keep the tel: CTA visible in the header at every breakpoint, and in the mobile sticky bar below md.
Do show gallery captions, metadata, and chip tags by default — never hover-only, since touch has no hover state.
Do disable the spark-gap arc, StatBar counters, and all scroll-reveal animation under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use green as a section background, a button fill, or body text — it is a logo accent, not a UI colour.
Don't reintroduce a green-950/green-900 surface step; they were deleted from the palette on purpose.
Don't reach for backdrop-filter on elements that aren't actually floating over something (the Earned Blur Rule) — PRODUCT.md rules out decorative glassmorphism by name.
Don't use background-clip: text, gradient text, or a saturated multi-stop gradient — this is an engineering brochure, not a SaaS landing page.
Don't use stock photography of "smiling guys in hardhats" — source real brochure/site photography of the actual substations, vans, and control room.

Don't build the projects gallery as Pinterest-style masonry, a uniform square-thumbnail grid, an autoplay carousel, a 50%-black-overlay-with-centered-title, or a flip/tilt hover card — all five are explicitly ruled out for this project.

Don't use a hero-metric template (big number, small label, gradient accent) — the StatBar is the one sanctioned numbers block, and its placeholder values stay marked as such until the client confirms them.
Don't let the eyebrow-dash pattern become the only section-opening device on a page — vary rhythm with StatBar, marquee, and full-bleed breaks (the Deliberate Eyebrow Rule).
